messages:
carla: Heads-up — I just saw plaintext user emails in the runtime request logs after the v1.3.4 deploy. Not sure how wide this is, tagging @dinesh @alice. Sample below from /var/log/serving/request.log:

```
2026-03-14T15:02:03Z INFO request_id=abc123 user_email=jon.smith@example.com model=redwood-base prompt_tokens=42
```

carla: I only noticed while doing a quick grep for `user_email=` while debugging a latency spike.

ops-bot: deploy:v1.3.4 finished on cluster-prod (ci-runner-12) :white_check_mark:

carla: This might be coming from the request-logger middleware — it logs metadata object which apparently contains user identifiers.

dinesh: Can you confirm exact path and run a count? also: do we have redaction config enabled on the logger?

carla: Path is `/var/log/serving/request.log` (rotated hourly). Running a quick ripgrep now: `rg "user_email=" /var/log/serving/request.log* | wc -l` — initial result: 12 matches across last 48h.

ben: if you can, run `rg -n -e "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+" /var/log/serving/request.log* --hidden` and `awk -F'user_email=' '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c` to see unique counts.

carla: Ran those — 12 matches, 8 of them are internal support aliases (support+prod@cust.com variants), 3 are real user emails, 1 looks like a service account email.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 (severity=P2) — reason: potential exposure of user identifiers in plaintext logs. Paging on-call.

alice: Ok. Stop any external exports of these logs immediately (S3 syncs / ETL jobs). @ops-bot can you disable the `log-export` lambda?

ops-bot: log-export lambda disabled by request of @alice :white_check_mark:

alice: Next steps: 1) snapshot current logs (preserve for forensics), 2) redact user identifiers in historical logs, 3) rotate any keys/tokens that may have been in those logs, 4) patch logger to strip PII and add unit tests, 5) review retention settings.

carla: Snapshotting to internal-incident-bucket now (upload started). Will share object key when done. Starting a purge/redaction job on the dev cluster to test.

elaine: Do we need to notify customers? any legal involvement?

alice: Don't send external comms yet. I'll loop in Legal and Privacy for scope & notification guidance. We'll triage impact first — how many unique real user accounts?

carla: Quick pivot: from those 3 real users, two are employees (test accounts) and one is an end-user. So current impact is 1 end-user in prod logs. However backups to s3 were happening until 09:00 UTC today (ops confirmed), so need to check bucket snapshots.

dinesh: For immediate mitigation, I pushed a tiny middleware patch to strip `user_email` before the logging call. Code (pseudocode):

```python
def redact_email(meta):
    if 'user_email' in meta:
        meta['user_email'] = '[REDACTED]'
    return meta

# apply before logger.info(...)
meta = redact_email(meta)
logger.info(..., extra=meta)
```

dinesh: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4092 — please review/approve for hotfix.

ben: I'll review PR in ~30m. If it's small and safe we should canary deploy to staging then prod quickly. If anyone hits blockers ping me.

carla: Actions (quick tracker):
- [x] stop external exports
- [ ] snapshot logs (in progress)
- [ ] run redaction on historical backups (queued)
- [ ] rotate any keys if found in logs
- [ ] merge hotfix and canary deploy

alice: For comms we need Legal sign-off. I'll open a ticket w/ privacy and draft a holding message. For now: no outbound customer emails until we confirm scope.

carla: Upload complete — bucket key: s3://internal-incident-bucket/INC-2026-0423/snapshot-1768501234.tar.gz

ben: Confirmed I can access snapshot for triage. Will run `rg` over the tarball in a temp workspace and report counts.

dinesh: Also adding an automated test to fail CI if `user_email` appears in any structured log message. Small follow-up in PR.

elaine: Thx all — please add me to the comms thread once Legal reviews.

alice: I'll update INC record when Legal weighs in. For now keep remediation channel-only and keep a concise timeline for postmortem.

carla: Will ping #incidents once we have final scope and recommended customer messaging. Also requesting reviewers for the PR: @ben, @alice, @dinesh.

ben: ACK, reviewing shortly.

carla: Quick note — log retention policy is 90 days; we should consider shortening and/or adding automatic redact step for metadata fields. Filing a follow-up RFC after this incident.

alice: Good. Thanks everyone — rounding up next steps and will post an incident summary when we have stable scope. :lock:
